title: Subsets, Set Laws & Set Proofs
goal: Tell `∈` from `⊆`, use the set laws, decide "true for all sets?" with a reason or one counterexample, and prove set identities by chasing elements.
magic: `∈`: is it listed? `⊆`: is everything inside it listed?
Set laws = logic laws with `∪ ∩ ᶜ`. `A \ B = A ∩ Bᶜ`.
False for all sets? One counterexample. True? A general argument.

blocks.title: 💡 Learn it, one idea at a time
Subsets: `⊆` allows equal, `⊂` doesn't
blocks.summary: `S ⊆ T`: every element of S is in T (S = T allowed). `S ⊂ T`: a subset that's strictly smaller. `∅ ⊆` everything.
blocks.picture: Your Spotify playlist and "all songs you've liked": every playlist song is liked, so playlist ⊆ liked. If there's at least one liked song not on the playlist, it's ⊂.
blocks.official: `S ⊆ T`: all elements of S are also elements of T; this **includes** `T ⊆ T` (Week 1, slide 30). `S ⊂ T`: a **proper** subset, `S ⊆ T` and `S ≠ T`. `∅ ⊆ X` for all sets `X`.

steps: Equal sets: `⊆` yes, but `⊂` needs a **strictly** bigger right side → **false**.
`∅` has no element that could fail → **true**.

tries.why: `∅ ⊆ ∅`, but they're equal, so not proper.

check.expr: not (set() < set())

tries.q: How many subsets `S` satisfy `S ⊆ {a, b}`? How many `S ⊂ {a, b}`?
tries.why: `∅, {a}, {b}, {a, b}`; the proper ones exclude `{a, b}` itself.

check.expr: len(Pow({'a','b'}))
len([S for S in Pow({'a','b'}) if S < frozenset({'a','b'})])

trap.correct: `⊆` allows equality (`X ⊆ X` always). Only `⊂` demands strictly smaller.

blocks.magic: `⊆` is like `≤`, `⊂` is like `<`. `∅ ⊆ X` always.

blocks.title: `∈` (is an element of) versus `⊆` (is a subset of)
blocks.summary: `x ∈ S`: `x` is one of the things listed. `X ⊆ S`: every thing **inside** `X` is listed in `S`.
blocks.picture: A bag of groceries S = {apple, {eggs}} where the eggs come in a carton. The apple ∈ S. The carton `{eggs}` ∈ S. But "eggs" alone is not an item in the bag: it's inside the carton.
blocks.official: An element of a set and a subset of that set are different concepts (Week 1, slide 30): `a ∈ {a, b}`, but `a ⊈ {a, b}`; `{a} ⊆ {a, b}`, but `{a} ∉ {a, b}`. To test `X ⊆ S`, check every element of `X` for `∈ S`.

steps: `{2}` is literally listed in S → `{2} ∈ S` **true**.
`{2} ⊆ S` needs `2 ∈ S`. The elements are `1`, `{2}`, `{1, 2}`; `2` alone isn't one → **false**.

tries.why: Note `{1, 2} ∈ S` is true, a different question.

check.expr: not ({1, 2} <= {1, frozenset({2}), frozenset({1, 2})})

tries.why: Its only element is `{2}`, and `{2} ∈ S`.

check.expr: {frozenset({2})} <= {1, frozenset({2}), frozenset({1, 2})}

tries.why: `∅` isn't listed as an element; but it's a subset of every set.

check.expr: frozenset() not in {1, 2}

trap.tempting: `{a} ⊆ S` and `{a} ∈ S` mean the same.
trap.correct: `{a} ⊆ S` asks whether `a ∈ S`. `{a} ∈ S` asks whether the set `{a}` itself is listed.
trap.test: For `⊆`, unwrap one layer of braces and check each element. For `∈`, look for the exact object.

blocks.magic: `∈`: is it listed? `⊆`: is everything inside it listed?

blocks.title: The set laws (and two useful extras)
blocks.summary: The same laws as logic, with `∪` for `∨`, `∩` for `∧`, `ᶜ` for `¬`. Plus `A \ B = A ∩ Bᶜ` and the complement laws.
blocks.picture: Venn diagrams are the "truth tables" of sets: each region is one row. If two expressions shade the same regions, they're equal.
blocks.official: Laws (Week 1, slide 29): commutativity, associativity, distribution (`A ∪ (B ∩ C) = (A ∪ B) ∩ (A ∪ C)`, `A ∩ (B ∪ C) = (A ∩ B) ∪ (A ∩ C)`), idempotence, identity `A ∪ ∅ = A`, `A ∩ ∅ = ∅`, double complementation `(Aᶜ)ᶜ = A`, De Morgan `(A ∪ B)ᶜ = Aᶜ ∩ Bᶜ`, `(A ∩ B)ᶜ = Aᶜ ∪ Bᶜ`. Facts (slide 30): `A ∪ B = B ⇔ A ⊆ B`, `A ∩ B = B ⇔ A ⊇ B`. ⚠️ Not on the slide but true and often needed: `A ∪ Aᶜ = U`, `A ∩ Aᶜ = ∅`, `A \ B = A ∩ Bᶜ`.

watch.answer: **`A`**: split A into "also in B" and "not in B", then glue back.

tries.why: De Morgan: `Aᶜ ∩ Bᶜ ∩ A`, and `Aᶜ ∩ A = ∅`.

check.expr: all(((U - (A | B)) & A) == set() for A in Pow(U) for B in Pow(U))

tries.q: Which law turns `(A ∩ B)ᶜ` into `Aᶜ ∪ Bᶜ`?

check.expr: all((U - (A & B)) == ((U - A) | (U - B)) for A in Pow(U) for B in Pow(U))

tries.q: `A ∪ B = B`. What can you conclude?
tries.why: Adding A to B changed nothing, so A was already inside B.

check.expr: all(((A | B) == B) == (A <= B) for A in Pow(U) for B in Pow(U))

trap.correct: De Morgan flips the operation: `(A ∪ B)ᶜ = Aᶜ ∩ Bᶜ`.

blocks.magic: Logic laws with `∪ ∩ ᶜ`. `A \ B = A ∩ Bᶜ`.

blocks.title: "True for all sets?": a reason, or ONE counterexample
blocks.summary: To show a set statement is false, one concrete example is enough. To show it's true, give a general reason.
blocks.picture: "Every swan is white": one black swan ends the debate. But you can't prove it true by showing a thousand white swans.
blocks.official: For claims "for all sets `A`, `B`": if **false**, give one specific counterexample (small sets like `A = B`, `A = ∅`, `A = {1}` usually do it). If **true**, argue with elements ("let `x ∈ …`") or with the laws. (This is the shape of Problem set 1, Q3 and Q6.)

watch.q: True for all sets? `(A \ B) ∪ B = A`.

tries.q: True for all sets? `A \ B ⊆ A`.
tries.why: Every element of `A \ B` is, by definition, in `A`.

check.expr: all((A - B) <= A for A in Pow(U) for B in Pow(U))

tries.q: True for all sets? `A ⊆ A ∩ B`.

check.expr: not all(A <= (A & B) for A in Pow(U) for B in Pow(U))

tries.why: An element of `B \ A` is not in `A`, so nothing can be in both.

check.expr: all((A & (B - A)) == set() for A in Pow(U) for B in Pow(U))

tries.q: True for all sets (universe `U`)? `(A ∩ B)ᶜ ⊆ Aᶜ`.
tries.why: The complement of a smaller set is **bigger**, so the inclusion goes the other way.

check.expr: not all((U - (A & B)) <= (U - A) for A in Pow(U) for B in Pow(U))

trap.tempting: Checking two examples that work proves it.
trap.correct: Examples can only **disprove**. A "for all" claim needs a general argument.
trap.test: True? Write "Let `x ∈ …`" and follow `x`. False? Find the smallest sets that break it.

blocks.magic: False: one counterexample. True: a general reason.

blocks.title: Proving `X = Y`: show `X ⊆ Y` and `Y ⊆ X`
blocks.summary: Take an arbitrary element of one side, show it's in the other. Then the reverse direction.
blocks.picture: Two guest lists are the same if everyone on list 1 is on list 2 AND everyone on list 2 is on list 1.
blocks.official: To prove a set identity without diagrams: (⊆) "Let `x ∈ X`. … so `x ∈ Y`." (⊇) "Let `x ∈ Y`. … so `x ∈ X`." Unfold each operation into logic: `x ∈ A ∪ B ⇔ x ∈ A or x ∈ B`; `x ∈ A ∩ B ⇔` and; `x ∈ A \ B ⇔ x ∈ A and x ∉ B`. (This is the method Problem set 1, Q5(b) asks for.) With Venn diagrams: shade both sides and compare regions.

steps: (⊆) Let `x ∈ A \ (B ∪ C)`. Then `x ∈ A` and `x ∉ B ∪ C`, i.e. `x ∉ B` and `x ∉ C`.
So `x ∈ A \ B` and `x ∈ A \ C`, i.e. `x ∈ (A \ B) ∩ (A \ C)`.
(⊇) Let `x ∈ (A \ B) ∩ (A \ C)`. Then `x ∈ A`, `x ∉ B`, `x ∉ C`.
So `x ∉ B ∪ C`, hence `x ∈ A \ (B ∪ C)`.
watch.answer: Both inclusions hold, so the sets are equal. (It's De Morgan in disguise.)

tries.q: Prove: if `A ⊆ B` then `A ∪ B = B`.
tries.a: (⊆) Let `x ∈ A ∪ B`. If `x ∈ A` then `x ∈ B` (since `A ⊆ B`); otherwise `x ∈ B` already. (⊇) If `x ∈ B` then `x ∈ A ∪ B`.
tries.why: Two directions, each a couple of lines.

check.expr: all((not (A <= B)) or ((A | B) == B) for A in Pow(U) for B in Pow(U))

tries.q: Prove `(A ∪ B)ᶜ = Aᶜ ∩ Bᶜ` by chasing elements.
tries.a: `x ∈ (A ∪ B)ᶜ` ⇔ `x ∉ A ∪ B` ⇔ not (`x ∈ A` or `x ∈ B`) ⇔ `x ∉ A` and `x ∉ B` ⇔ `x ∈ Aᶜ ∩ Bᶜ`.
tries.why: A chain of `⇔` proves both directions at once; the middle step is logic's De Morgan.

check.expr: all((U - (A | B)) == ((U - A) & (U - B)) for A in Pow(U) for B in Pow(U))

tries.a: `x ∈ A \ (B ∩ C)` ⇔ `x ∈ A` and not (`x ∈ B` and `x ∈ C`) ⇔ `x ∈ A` and (`x ∉ B` or `x ∉ C`) ⇔ (`x ∈ A`, `x ∉ B`) or (`x ∈ A`, `x ∉ C`) ⇔ `x ∈ (A \ B) ∪ (A \ C)`.

check.expr: all((A - (B & C)) == ((A - B) | (A - C)) for A in Pow(U) for B in Pow(U) for C in Pow(U))

trap.tempting: Prove only one direction (`X ⊆ Y`) and conclude `X = Y`.
trap.correct: Equality needs **both** `X ⊆ Y` and `Y ⊆ X` (or a chain of `⇔`).

blocks.magic: Equality = two inclusions. Unfold each operation into and/or/not.

blocks.title: Cardinalities: `|A ∪ B| = |A| + |B| − |A ∩ B|`
blocks.summary: Adding `|A|` and `|B|` counts the overlap twice, so subtract it once.
blocks.picture: 30 people like cats, 25 like dogs, 10 like both. At least one: `30 + 25 − 10 = 45`.
blocks.official: Lecture exercise 1.4.8 (Week 1, slide 33): `|A ∪ B| = |A| + |B| − |A ∩ B|`, hence `|A ∪ B| + |A ∩ B| = |A| + |B|`; `|A \ B| = |A| − |A ∩ B|`; `|A ⊕ B| = |A| + |B| − 2|A ∩ B|`.

watch.q: A class of 40: 25 know Java, 18 know Python, 10 know both. How many know neither?

tries.q: Same class: how many know Java but not Python?
Same class: how many know exactly one of the two?

trap.correct: Only if A and B are disjoint. Otherwise subtract the overlap `|A ∩ B|`.
trap.test: Draw the Venn diagram and count the middle region once.

blocks.magic: Add, then subtract the double-counted overlap.

items.a: **Not meaningful / false:** `3` is not a set here, so ask `3 ∈ {1, 2, 3}` (true) instead.
items.why: `⊆` compares a set with a set; `∈` compares an element with a set.
Equal, so not a proper subset.

items.q: Name the law: `A ∩ A = A`.

check.expr: all((A & A) == A for A in Pow(U))

items.q: Simplify `(Aᶜ)ᶜ ∪ ∅`.

check.expr: all(((U - (U - A)) | set()) == A for A in Pow(U))

items.q: True for all sets? `|A \ B| ≤ |A|`.
items.why: `A \ B ⊆ A`, and a subset can't have more elements.

check.expr: all(len(A - B) <= len(A) for A in Pow(U) for B in Pow(U))

items.q: True for all sets? `A ∪ (B ∩ A) = A`.
items.why: `B ∩ A ⊆ A`, so adding it to A changes nothing.

check.expr: all((A | (B & A)) == A for A in Pow(U) for B in Pow(U))

items.q: True for all sets? `|A ⊕ B| ≤ |A ∪ B|`.

check.expr: all(len(A ^ B) <= len(A | B) for A in Pow(U) for B in Pow(U))
frozenset() in {frozenset(), frozenset({1})}
not ({1} <= {frozenset(), frozenset({1})})
{frozenset({1})} <= {frozenset(), frozenset({1})}

items.q: Simplify `(A ∪ B) ∩ (A ∪ Bᶜ)`.

check.expr: all(((A | B) & (A | (U - B))) == A for A in Pow(U) for B in Pow(U))

blocks.sub: Problem set 1, Q3 and Q5 style: true for all sets (reason or counterexample), and element-chasing proofs. Original statements.

items.q: Which statements are true for **all** sets `A`, `B` (universe `U`)?
items.why: (1) and (3) follow from the definitions. (2) fails for `A = {1}`, `B = ∅`. (4) fails for `A = ∅`, `B = {1}`. (5) is `A ∩ Bᶜ ⊆ A`.

exprs: all((A & B) <= (A | B) for A in Pow(U) for B in Pow(U))
all(A <= (A & B) for A in Pow(U) for B in Pow(U))
all((A & (B - A)) == set() for A in Pow(U) for B in Pow(U))
all(((A - B) | B) == A for A in Pow(U) for B in Pow(U))
all((A - B) <= (U - B) for A in Pow(U) for B in Pow(U))

items.q: True for all sets? If false, give a counterexample: `A ∪ (B \ C) = (A ∪ B) \ C`.
items.why: The right side removes C's elements from A too; the left doesn't.

check.expr: not all((A | (B - C)) == ((A | B) - C) for A in Pow(U) for B in Pow(U) for C in Pow(U))

items.q: Prove `A ∩ (B \ C) = (A ∩ B) \ C` by chasing elements.
items.a: `x ∈ A ∩ (B \ C)` ⇔ `x ∈ A` and `x ∈ B` and `x ∉ C` ⇔ `x ∈ A ∩ B` and `x ∉ C` ⇔ `x ∈ (A ∩ B) \ C`.
items.why: Unfold, regroup the "and"s, fold back up.

check.expr: all((A & (B - C)) == ((A & B) - C) for A in Pow(U) for B in Pow(U) for C in Pow(U))

items.q: Prove: `A ⊆ B` implies `Bᶜ ⊆ Aᶜ`.
items.a: Let `x ∈ Bᶜ`, so `x ∉ B`. If `x` were in `A`, then `x ∈ B` (as `A ⊆ B`), contradiction. So `x ∉ A`, i.e. `x ∈ Aᶜ`.
items.why: It's the contrapositive of "`x ∈ A ⇒ x ∈ B`".

check.expr: all((not (A <= B)) or ((U - B) <= (U - A)) for A in Pow(U) for B in Pow(U))

items.q: When exactly is `(A ∪ B) \ C = A ∪ (B \ C)`?
items.why: `(A ∪ B) \ C = (A \ C) ∪ (B \ C)`. For it to equal `A ∪ (B \ C)`, no element of A may be removed by C, i.e. `A ∩ C = ∅`. Conversely, if `A ∩ C = ∅` then `A \ C = A`. (Same kind of question as the lecture's 1.8.2(b).)

check.expr: all((((A | B) - C) == (A | (B - C))) == (len(A & C) == 0) for A in Pow(U) for B in Pow(U) for C in Pow(U))

items.q: When exactly is `A ⊕ B = A ∪ B`?
items.why: `A ⊕ B = (A ∪ B) \ (A ∩ B)`, so they're equal iff the overlap is empty.

check.expr: all(((A ^ B) == (A | B)) == (len(A & B) == 0) for A in Pow(U) for B in Pow(U))

items.q: When exactly is `A \ B = B \ A`?
items.why: `A \ B ⊆ A` and `B \ A ⊆ B` are disjoint (nothing is in both A and not-A). Equal disjoint sets must both be `∅`, which means `A ⊆ B` and `B ⊆ A`.

check.expr: all(((A - B) == (B - A)) == (A == B) for A in Pow(U) for B in Pow(U))

items.q: In `[1, 100]`, 50 numbers are even, 33 are multiples of 3, 16 are multiples of 6. Using set sizes only, how many are **odd and not multiples of 3**?

check.expr: sum(1 for n in range(1, 101) if n % 2 and n % 3)
frozenset({'a'}) not in {'a', 'b'}

items.q: True for all sets? `A ∩ B ⊆ B`.

check.expr: all((A & B) <= B for A in Pow(U) for B in Pow(U))

items.q: To prove `X = Y` by elements, what two things do you show?

lines: `S ⊆ T`: every element of S is in T (equality allowed). `S ⊂ T`: proper.
Laws: commutative, associative, distributive, idempotent, identity, double complement, De Morgan; `A ∪ B = B ⇔ A ⊆ B`.
Element chasing: unfold `∪ ∩ \ ᶜ` into or / and / not, then fold back.
